cards.title: pcVPC for Adaptive Dose Adjustments
cards.claim: pcVPCs are readily applicable to data from studies with a priori or a posteriori dose adaptations (e.g., therapeutic drug monitoring), where traditional VPCs can be misleading or uninformative due to the correlation between dose adjustments and the dependent variable.
conditions: Study design involves dose adjustments based on observed concentrations or other dependent variable-related factors.
The dose adjustment algorithm may not be well-documented or fully reproducible in simulations.
Traditional VPCs show decreasing observed variability over time due to dose adjustments, which is not captured by simulations using realized designs.
required_inputs: Model predictions for the realized design.
Identification of bins for prediction correction.
limitations: Simulations based on realized designs do not maintain the correlation between dose alterations and previous observed concentrations, which pcVPC corrects for.
If a dose adjustment algorithm is simulated, it may not accurately mimic real-life adjustments, leading to deceptive results; pcVPC based on realized design is preferred in these cases.
cards.downstream_use: Validating model predictive performance in clinical or preclinical studies with adaptive dosing protocols, ensuring that observed variability is correctly attributed to random effects rather than design artifacts.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
